children.text:
>Why do we assume humans will do the work?

I suppose, at that point, the key inputs to a company become creativity and ambition (rather than, say, overall effort). Humans are still better at those than AI.

Humans would still direct branding/marketing/positioning while we control the overall creativity and ambition of a project/company.

If the only intent is to make money, then I suppose you could build machines that tweak the creativity & ambition in different ways to create different products & services, in which case you can argue no humans need to be in the loop.

Why do we assume humans will do the work? What's the inherent reason for this?

What I'm saying isn't anything new. It was a hot topic during abd after imdustrial revolution. Even Karl Marx joined the discussion and wrote about it. The key thing is, what is money and what determines the prices. If there's abundance, the problems you talked about start to occur and market cannot price the goods. This is, to some, abundance communism.

children.text: If you invest into/found a company to pay for the robots and tokens, you'll probably want to give it a specific direction instead of a random one. But yes, all the rest can probably be automated.

children.author: jameslk
children.text:
Marketing, branding, positioning are part of a zero sum game, so cannot be automated with the same AI model, otherwise you lose differentiation

Patents, regulations are decided by humans because we’re ruled by humans

> Branding, marketing, positioning, patents, regulations, etc. Who does that work?

Why are humans needed for that?

source.text:
> In a fully mechanized/automated world, we won't work. It will make no sense to work.

Your entire argument rests of this statement. Why wouldn't it make sense to work? How would one company differentiate its products from another if they're all using the same AI?

Let's take a contrived example. Let's say automation can produce yachts for all of us at affordable prices someday. We're just going to all own yachts then. What will be the reason for one person to choose one yacht over another? Branding, marketing, positioning, patents, regulations, etc. Who does that work? Humans. Because ultimately you're selling to humans in a human-controlled world, not machines.
